name: Zolpidem
description: Zolpidem (Ambien) facts: use for insomnia, different doses for women and men, complex sleep behavior warning, interactions, overdose, withdrawal, and legal access.
quick: Zolpidem (Ambien) is a prescription sleep medicine that acts on the same brain receptors as benzodiazepines. It is a Schedule IV controlled substance. Its boxed warning covers complex sleep behaviors such as sleepwalking and sleep-driving, and women are prescribed lower doses because they clear it more slowly.

blocks.p: Zolpidem is approved for short-term treatment of insomnia with difficulty falling asleep. Extended-release zolpidem also helps people stay asleep, and low-dose sublingual zolpidem is for waking in the middle of the night with at least four hours left in bed.[[1]]

The figures below come from the FDA-approved label and describe how prescribers typically use zolpidem. They are not personal dosing advice. A prescriber sets the dose for each person and adjusts it over time.[[1]]
In 2013 the FDA lowered the recommended dose for women after studies showed many still had enough zolpidem in their blood the next morning to impair driving.[[1]]
Take it only when you can stay in bed for a full 7 to 8 hours.

sections.q: What are the risks and side effects of zolpidem?

boxed.title: FDA boxed warning
items: Complex sleep behaviors, including sleepwalking, sleep-driving, and other activities while not fully awake, have caused serious injuries and deaths. Stop the medicine if one occurs, and do not take it if you have had one before.[[2]]

blocks.p: **Common side effects** include drowsiness, dizziness, headache, diarrhea, and a "drugged" feeling. Next-morning impairment can affect driving even when the person feels awake.[[1]]
**Other risks** include memory loss for events after a dose, abnormal thinking and behavior, worsening depression, and dependence with long-term use.[[1]]

sections.q: What does zolpidem overdose look like?

blocks.p: Zolpidem overdose causes deep sleepiness progressing to coma. Breathing problems are more likely when it is combined with alcohol, opioids, or other sedatives.[[1]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, hard to wake, or breathing slowly.
For advice when the person is awake and stable, call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222 (US, free, 24 hours).
If opioids could be involved, including pills not from a pharmacy, give naloxone if you have it. Naloxone does not reverse zolpidem, but it will not harm the person.
Stay with the person and place them on their side if they are drowsy or vomiting.

sections.q: What is zolpidem withdrawal like, and how long does it last?

blocks.p: After regular use, stopping zolpidem can cause rebound insomnia and, less often, withdrawal symptoms such as anxiety, shakiness, sweating, and, rarely, seizures after high-dose use.[[1]]

timeline.title: Rebound insomnia
timeline.text: Worse sleep than before treatment for a few nights.

timeline.title: Withdrawal in long-term users
timeline.text: Anxiety, irritability, tremor, sweating, and nausea.

blocks.p: People who have taken zolpidem nightly for months should taper with their prescriber rather than stop suddenly.

sections.q: How do you get zolpidem legally in the US?

blocks.p: In the United States, zolpidem is a Schedule IV controlled substance. The only legal way to get it is with a prescription from a clinician registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), filled by a licensed pharmacy. Depending on state law, that can be a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.[[3]]

ul: **Refills:** a Schedule IV prescription can be refilled up to five times within six months of the date it was written. After that, a new prescription is needed.[[4]]

**Telehealth:** federal flexibilities let DEA-registered clinicians prescribe Schedule II to V medicines after a telemedicine visit, without a prior in-person exam, through December 31, 2026. A permanent DEA rule was under final review in late 2026. State rules can be stricter.[[5]]
**Monitoring:** prescribers and pharmacists in most states check a prescription drug monitoring program, a database of controlled-substance prescriptions, before prescribing or dispensing.

**Pharmacies:** a legitimate pharmacy always requires a valid prescription, has a licensed pharmacist available, and is licensed in the state it ships to. The FDA's BeSafeRx tool and the NABP's safe pharmacy list help confirm a pharmacy is real.[[6]][[7]]

blocks.p: **Traveling:** keep the medicine in its original pharmacy container and carry a copy of the prescription. Check the rules of the destination country before travel, because many countries restrict controlled medicines or require a permit.

Yes, but only with a valid prescription and only from a pharmacy licensed in your state. Many licensed pharmacies, including mail-order pharmacies run by insurers, fill zolpidem prescriptions online and ship them. Buying zolpidem from a website that does not require a prescription is illegal, and the product is often fake.[[6]][[8]]

steps: A clinician evaluates you in person or by telemedicine and decides whether zolpidem is appropriate.
The prescription goes to a pharmacy
Prescriptions for controlled medicines are usually sent electronically, straight from the prescriber to the pharmacy you choose.
The pharmacy checks and fills it
A pharmacist verifies the prescription and your identity, then dispenses the medicine in person or by mail.

blocks.p: **Signs that an online seller is illegal:**

ul: It sells zolpidem with no prescription, or after only a short online questionnaire.
It takes orders through social media, messaging apps, or email.
It asks for payment in cryptocurrency, gift cards, or money transfers.
It has no US street address, no state pharmacy license, and no pharmacist to speak to.
Its prices are far below those of ordinary pharmacies, or it ships from another country.

blocks.p: The FDA's BeSafeRx tool links to each state's license lookup, and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy lists verified online pharmacies.[[6]][[7]]

faq: Why do women get a lower Ambien dose?
Women clear zolpidem more slowly, so the same dose leaves more drug in the blood the next morning and can impair driving.
No, but it works on the same GABA-A receptors and has similar risks of dependence and withdrawal.
Doing activities while not fully awake, such as walking, cooking, or driving, without remembering it later. They can cause serious injuries.
How long does zolpidem stay in your system?
Its half-life is about 2.5 hours, and most is gone within a day.
